title: 3D Rotation
description: A 3d rotation camera treats the figure as a sculptural object on a virtual turntable of space. The world may be a cyc or a void; the point is every side, not a street orbit.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Show every side. Inspection, toys, a character as merchandise: even lighting or studio, the person as a model.
Combine with a computed look if they should feel rendered. A chase does not want a turntable.
A 360 walk around a street is an orbit: walls and extras shear in a real room. This is product-space.
A slight arc is not enough; we should sense the back will arrive.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Virtual camera on a circular or spherical spline, subject locked, often studio or void. One axis unless you mean a tumble.
Prompt: 3D rotation around [Subject], a turntable of space, the figure as a sculptural object in orbit.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: Product films are the native grammar. The Matrix freeze-turn is the narrative cousin: a body as a sculpture in computed space.
Use the grammar, not the frame.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is a slight arc in a street. The tell: a living room shears a little and we never see the back.
The fix: full turntable energy, subject as sculpture, studio or void, the back will arrive.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is 3D Rotation in film?
3D rotation treats the figure as a sculptural object on a virtual turntable of space, often in a studio or void, so every side can be shown.
3D Rotation vs Lazy Susan
A lazy susan often turns a physical object while the camera stays put. 3D rotation is a virtual camera orbiting a figure as a model in computed or studio space.
When should I use 3D Rotation?
Use it to inspect a person or prop as an object. Do not use it for a chase or a real-room conversation.
How do I prompt 3D Rotation for AI image or video?
Write a virtual turntable and the figure as sculpture. Example: 3D rotation around [Subject], a turntable of space, the figure as a sculptural object in orbit.
